source.title: Capability Ceilings in Autoregressive Language Models: Empirical Evidence from Knowledge-Intensive Tasks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; it is not garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates downstream task performance across model scales and reports that MMLU accuracy stagnates despite decreasing task cross-entropy, while arithmetic accuracy improves. This refines the scope of downstream predictability; it does not directly fit or test pretraining-loss power laws or compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports task-level accuracy and cross-entropy across model sizes, which bear on V6. Its task cross-entropy is not held-out pretraining loss, and the paper does not fit power laws or test extrapolation. The attention-pattern swaps in Table 2 are not results on scale-based downstream predictability, so they are left out.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates OPT (125M-30B) and Pythia (70M-6.9B) on MMLU math, arithmetic and QQP. It reports that task cross-entropy falls smoothly with scale while accuracy stays flat on MMLU, saturates on QQP and rises on arithmetic. It argues that downstream predictability from scale or loss needs restating per task. It fits no power laws and runs no pretraining-loss or compute-allocation experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that scaling OPT and Pythia lowers task cross-entropy smoothly but does not raise MMLU math accuracy, which stays at 19-20% (below chance), so loss alone masks capability stagnation. Arithmetic scales conventionally and QQP saturates. They say scaling beyond 1-2B gives minimal knowledge-task gains in these families. They leave open whether this holds for other architectures.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates downstream task accuracy and task-level cross-entropy over pretrained model families; it does not use held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws, or test compute-optimal training. The paper does not state a reproduction of the original methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported downstream scaling outcome varies by task: MMLU accuracy stagnates, arithmetic accuracy improves, and QQP accuracy scales minimally.

fits_no_version.finding: Swapping attention patterns between OPT-2.7B and OPT-6.7B collapses MMLU accuracy (up to -100%) and degrades arithmetic accuracy (up to -86%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned attention patterns in differently sized models are not interchangeable; knowledge-task performance is brittle to cross-model attention transplant.

record.problems: The evidence covers only OPT and Pythia and selected tasks. The paper reports no quantitative uncertainty estimates; Pythia-specific per-scale results are not provided in the text. It does not fit or evaluate power-law predictions.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 attention-pattern intervention results are omitted because they test the effect of swapping attention patterns, not downstream performance scaling or its predictability.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fit in parameters, tokens or compute.
No controlled shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer.
No prediction of downstream performance from pretraining loss, no fitted downstream scaling law, and no quantitative extrapolation. The results are only qualitative trends over model size.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Pythia results for arithmetic and QQP accuracy and for task loss. The text says only that the pattern is consistent across both families; no numbers are given.
Confidence-competence gap ratio: about 48 for MMLU versus about 0.26 for arithmetic, quantifying loss-accuracy decoupling.
Claim that accuracy gains on knowledge tasks become minimal beyond 1-2B parameters; no per-scale table supports it.

record.verdict_notes: Single-author preprint with an evaluation set of 250 items per task and no uncertainty estimates. The Table 2 baselines (MMLU 0.500/0.438, arithmetic 0.100/0.700 for OPT-2.7B/6.7B) are inconsistent with the flat 19-20% MMLU and the monotone arithmetic curves reported elsewhere. This casts doubt on the reliability of the main rows. MMLU below chance may reflect answer-format or scoring artefacts the paper does not examine.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss power-law fit in parameters, tokens, or compute; the reported losses are task-level cross-entropy.
No small-run fits or predictions of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling experiments.
Tests selected downstream tasks across model scale, but not downstream prediction from held-out pretraining loss or quantitative extrapolation from smaller runs.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, compute-optimal splits, or departures from fitted power-law curves.

rows.subject: OPT models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated MMLU mathematics accuracy across model sizes.
rows.note: The authors describe the accuracy variation as within measurement noise and effectively constant across the scale range.
rows.check: Baseline should be the smallest OPT model's accuracy, not 25% random chance. Chance is a reference level, not the scaling baseline. The paper's own Table 2 gives MMLU accuracy 0.500 and 0.438 for OPT-2.7B/6.7B, which contradicts the 19-20% flat figure. Treat the value with caution.

rows.subject: OPT models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured MMLU mathematics task cross-entropy across model sizes.
rows.note: This is task-level cross-entropy, not held-out pretraining loss.
rows.check: Task-level cross-entropy on MMLU answers, not pretraining loss. It bears on V6 only as a continuous downstream metric. The 3.1→2.1 endpoints are given in Section 1.1 without naming a family; Table 1 (OPT) gives -31.1%.

rows.subject: OPT models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated arithmetic accuracy across model sizes.
rows.note: The authors characterize arithmetic as conventional scaling, with accuracy improving as loss improves.
rows.check: Endpoints are 2.4%→31% in the text but 2%→31% in Section 4.1. Table 2 baselines (0.100 for OPT-6.7B, 0.700 for OPT-2.7B) conflict with monotone arithmetic scaling.

rows.subject: OPT models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured arithmetic task cross-entropy across model sizes.
rows.note: The paper does not give the endpoint loss values in the table.

rows.subject: OPT models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated QQP paraphrase-detection accuracy across model sizes.
rows.value: Accuracy fluctuates around 60%; Table 1 reports ∆ Acc -1.3%.
rows.note: The authors describe this as minimal scaling.
rows.check: Baseline not stated; the authors label the result saturated performance (around 60%), not a failure below chance.

rows.subject: OPT models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured QQP task cross-entropy across model sizes.
rows.note: The paper does not give the endpoint loss values in the table.

rows.subject: Pythia models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated MMLU mathematics accuracy across model sizes.
rows.note: No Pythia-specific per-scale values are stated; the paper describes the pattern as consistent across OPT and Pythia.
rows.check: Baseline should be the smallest Pythia model, not 25% chance. No Pythia per-scale numbers are given; the value comes from abstract and caption wording that pools both families.

relationships.condition: MMLU mathematics accuracy, OPT and Pythia
relationships.reason: Accuracy stays at 19.2-20.4% across 240× scale, below chance, while task loss falls 31% (R1, R7, R2). Small samples (250 items) and the Table 2 inconsistency weaken this.
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy stayed at 19.2–20.4% across 240× scale while task loss fell 31%, although the 250-item samples and inconsistent table weaken the evidence.

relationships.reason: Accuracy hovers near 60% (∆ -1.3%) while task loss falls 16.3%; the authors call this saturation at small scale (R5, R6).
relationships.display_finding: Accuracy stayed near 60%, changing by −1.3%, while task loss fell 16.3%.

relationships.reason: Accuracy rises from 2.4% to 31% as task loss falls 26.6% (R3, R4).
relationships.display_finding: Arithmetic accuracy rises from 2.4% to 31% as task loss decreases by 26.6%.

relationships.condition: Task cross-entropy on all three tasks, OPT (and Pythia per Figure 2)
relationships.reason: Task loss decreases smoothly with scale on every task (R2, R4, R6).
relationships.display_finding: Task cross-entropy decreases smoothly with scale on all three tasks for OPT and Pythia.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
